_comment: The install manifest, <install root>/.claude/fleet.json (the root of the repository your
agents work in). `fleet adopt <install root>` writes it from the fleet's
templates/fleet.example.json when the repository has none, and never over an existing one.
Fill it in: replace every value that is a <placeholder> as a whole, and review the rest:
each is an example or a fleet default.
JSON has no comments, so every key starting with _ is documentation the loader strips.
Check the result with `fleet settings`: it prints the manifest with the fleet defaults
applied, or names the key it refuses. A value still in the placeholder form (one <...>
with a space inside) is refused; a placeholder inside a doc path, such as <feature-slug>,
is filled in when it is read.
schema: always 1 for this fleet version.
skills: the fleet skills `fleet link` links into each agent's .claude/skills/. It must
include chat-transport and the skill of every enabled transport (slack-communication for
slack). Remove a skill to stop linking it.
Required keys: schema, fleet, skills, transports. Every other key is optional; an absent
key takes the fleet default shown in CONVENTIONS.md.
repo: the fleet repository's clone URL. min_tag: the oldest fleet release this install
works with; `fleet link`, `fleet status` and `fleet upgrade` refuse an older host checkout.
enabled: the chat transports your agents use; each must be a WORKING transport of the fleet
(placeholders such as discord and telegram are refused). default: the transport an address
or a claim without one uses; it must be in enabled.
How your install does the development steps fleet skills refer to by key. A value is
{"skill": "<name>"} (load that skill) or {"doc": "<repo-relative path>"} (read that file;
<placeholders> allowed), either with an optional "section", or null. Absent or null means
your install has no such convention: the reading skill skips that step and says so.
A skill is the install's own .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; `fleet settings` refuses a
skill or a doc path (placeholders aside) that names no file in the install.
people_notes is where your install records standing requests from people, such as a
person who wants every open question collected into one daily digest.
The keys and who reads them: CONVENTIONS.md.
The fleet's house rules, set to their fleet defaults here; change a value to change the rule.
questions_per_message: how many questions an agent may put to a person in one message.
state_the_fact: write the current state, not its history (true or false).
ascii_skill_prose: skill prose is plain ASCII (true or false).
Each rule and its default: CONVENTIONS.md.
When an agent re-asks a person about an open blocker: every every_minutes (a divisor of
1440) on the given days (mon..sun), from start to end (24-hour HH:MM, start before end),
in the IANA time zone tz.
cities: the clocks a reported time is rendered in, in this order. name is what the reader
sees; tz is an IANA time zone. Replace the example cities with your readers' cities.
Where credential files live. The order: $FLEET_SECRETS_DIR, else the environment variable
named by legacy_env (set it when your machines already export another variable for this
directory; null when they do not), else default_dir. Paths may use ~, $VAR and
${VAR:-default}.
Only for an install whose agents contribute to the fleet repository.
identity: the public name and e-mail every fleet commit is made with.
deny_list: the private list of values the commit gate refuses (path relative to the
install root), or null to state the install has no private values. `fleet settings`
refuses a path with no file there.
outside_pr_reviewer: the person who reviews and merges pull requests from outside
contributors; agents never review them.

identity._comment: Use an address you are happy to publish, such as a GitHub no-reply address.
identity.name: <Your Name>

upstream.outside_pr_reviewer: <the person who reviews outside pull requests>
